_description: Re-measurement of the 5 proposed fixes from the 2026-10-01 pi5_benchmark run, on the same Raspberry Pi 5 Model B Rev 1.0. Each value below was actually run, not estimated.

ocr_decoder.hypothesis: greedy decoder should be faster than beamsearch (beamWidth=5)
ocr_decoder.result: regressed - greedy measured slower, not faster
ocr_decoder.note: The ~19s cost is EasyOCR's text-detector network on CPU, not the beam-search decode step, so the decoder flag doesn't touch the actual bottleneck. config.OCR_DECODER left at 'beamsearch' (env-overridable).

bn.reason: piper 2023.11.14-2 (only prebuilt ARM64 release) throws 'Phonemes must be one codepoint' on bn_BD-google-medium.onnx (e.g. the diphthong "aɪ" is not a single codepoint in this binary's phoneme id map) and aborts. utils.TTSEngine._piper() now checks piper's return code and falls back to espeak-ng, so Bangla still speaks - just at the unchanged espeak-ng speed.

playback_fix.problem: On this headless Pi 5 (no display attached), PipeWire has nothing to route the HDMI ALSA device to, so 'aplay' fails to open it (error 524) on every call - and neither that failure nor the piper crash above raised a Python exception, so TTSEngine._piper() would previously return having played nothing at all, silently.
playback_fix.fix: utils.TTSEngine._audio_player_cmd() probes 'aplay' then 'pw-cat' once per process and caches whichever one actually opens the device; _piper() also now checks piper_proc.returncode and raises (triggering the espeak-ng fallback) instead of assuming success.

object_mode.before: skipped - no YOLOv8 COCO weights in this checkout

watermark_localizer.claim_checked: live app already uses the learned localizer, not SIFT, by default
watermark_localizer.evidence: WatermarkChecker.localizer loads whenever config.WATERMARK_LOCALIZER_PATH exists (it does); genuine_prob() calls _window_learned() first and only falls back to SIFT when that returns None. The benchmark's 372ms 'watermark_int8_sift' entry forced checker.localizer=None for comparison - it does not reflect live app behavior.

currency_int8.claim_checked: live app already loads best_int8.onnx on Pi 5, not best.pt
currency_int8.evidence: config.CURRENCY_YOLO_PATH already selects best_int8.onnx when config.ON_RASPBERRY_PI_5 is true, and _candidate_yolo_paths() inserts it first. Confirmed by live log on this device: 'Currency YOLO loaded from .../best_int8.onnx'. The benchmark's separate taka_yolo_pt/taka_yolo_onnx_fp32 entries are explicit comparison loads, not what currency_mode_full actually runs.

ocr_capture.change: process_frame unchanged; TTS confirmation now via Piper (en-us)

currency.change: unchanged - both inference (already int8) and TTS (Bangla, still espeak-ng) are the same path as before
